title: The kitchen floor
intake: Adult female, 81, found on her kitchen floor at 09:00 by her daughter.
context: She lived alone and was independent. Her daughter came by because she didn't answer the phone that morning.

procedures.name: Scene investigation
procedures.blurb: The kitchen, her medicines, who spoke to her last.

procedures.name: External exam
procedures.blurb: Examine the body region by region.

procedures.name: Toxicology (rush)
procedures.blurb: Drugs and alcohol in the blood.

findings.label: Last call
findings.text: Daughter: they spoke by phone at 20:30, and she sounded well.

findings.label: Kitchen
findings.text: Tiled floor. A small rug is rucked up by her feet and a cup of tea is spilled beside her. Nothing else is out of place.
findings.meaning: The scene fits a trip and a fall, with no sign of a struggle.

findings.label: Blood thinner
findings.text: Warfarin in the medicine cabinet, refilled last week.
findings.meaning: Warfarin slows clotting, so a head injury that would be minor for most people can cause a large bleed.

findings.label: Rigor
findings.text: Fully stiff in all major joints.
findings.meaning: Rigor is complete: roughly 7.5 hours or more.

findings.label: Livor
findings.text: Purple-red on the back; does not blanch under pressure.
findings.meaning: Fixed livor: roughly 8 hours or more. It matches the position she was found in, so she wasn't moved.

findings.label: Back of head
findings.text: A bruise and swelling on the back of the head, low down at the level of a hat brim. No other head injuries.
findings.meaning: One impact at hat-brim level on the back of the head: the typical injury of a backward fall.

findings.label: Forearms
findings.text: No bruises on the hands or forearms.
findings.meaning: No defense injuries, so nothing suggests she was fending off blows.

findings.label: Brain
findings.text: A large subdural hematoma (a blood clot over the brain), and bruising of the front of the brain, opposite the impact.
findings.meaning: Bruising opposite the impact (contrecoup) means a moving head struck a fixed surface: a fall, not a blow. The clot is the cause of death.

findings.label: Heart
findings.text: Mildly enlarged heart; coronary arteries 40% narrowed.
findings.meaning: Common at her age, and not severe enough to explain a sudden death.

findings.label: Toxicology
findings.text: Warfarin at a therapeutic level; no alcohol or other drugs.
findings.meaning: Taken as prescribed: not an overdose, but enough to make the bleed much worse.

causes.label: Subdural hematoma from blunt head injury in a fall
Stroke from bleeding inside the brain (disease)

person: Eleanor Voss, 81, a former school librarian who still walked to the market every morning.
story: She tripped on the rug at about 21:15 and fell backward, striking her head on the tiles. On warfarin, the bleed over her brain grew quickly. Her death is certified an accident: the fall caused the injury, even though the medicine made it worse.
